articleTitle: Predicting Diabetes Status Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: One of the most severe public health issues affecting the global population today is that of diabetes. Diabetes prediction has remained the challenging aspect of managing this illness with the need for timely diagnosis and treatment. This study presents the classification of diabetes status based on the BRFSS2015 data using the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model. The results revealed that MLP can classify diabetes with 74.1 % accuracy and AVC of 82.2%. The variable relevance chart showed that the most highly relevant variables for predicting diabetes are physiological factors like BMI, self-reported physical health status, self-reported mental health status, blood pressure, income, age, etc. On the other hand, smoking, eating vegetables, exercising, and eating fruits are considered less necessary for predicting the disease. The reverse holds for the different lifestyle changes, such as diet and physical exercise, which made it clear that people were at risk factor for diabetes through physiological parameters. This indicates difficulty in classifying diabetes risk factors and the need for adequate diagnostic measures. Such an approach will allow for avoiding unnecessary treatment expenses and increasing people's productivity. Future research should look into how the individual variables interact with one another to enhance the predictive models and derive pertinent public health interventions.

articleTitle: Improvement of K-Means Clustering Through Center's Hybrid Initialization
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: This paper evaluates the effect of initial center selection on cluster quality and the rate of convergence in K-means clustering. In this paper, a new approach is proposed that uses random initialization and spatial distribution scores. The main objective is to enhance K-means clustering by creating a simple, novel, and efficient technique shredded for data classification and other high-level image processing tasks. Our approach relies on image color segmentation through the application of a transformation to the image's RGB color space, representing every pixel by three values of different components of color, divided into blocks, and then a calculation of the density of dots in every block. This value of density mark provided information about the distribution of color values around various parts of an image. It uses a tactical approach in selecting initial centers, namely Scored Centers Initialization, or SCI. It chooses the block with the highest score as the initial center block chosen randomly. Then, it selects subsequent centers based on the probability assessed by the Euclidean distance from the nearest one picked center and the density score of the block. It continuously does this until the desired number of centers is reached. The experimental results indicate that the clustering effect of the approach proposed was better than the traditional Random Centers Initialization method, thus proving the proposed strategy was effective. Based on the consideration of point-to-center distances and the spatial distribution score, it captured better data structures to get quicker convergence and higher quality in the cluster assignment.

articleTitle: Navigating Ethical and Practical Limitations of Advancing Surgical Care Through AI
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The technological revolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) aims to simulate human intelligence through machines such as computer systems. As we have begun integrating AI into our daily lives, it also opens a new world of opportunity in the medical field. Despite that, AI continues to raise concerns about the ethical and practical limitations associated with its use in medicine, particularly in its use before, during, and after surgery. Through a comprehensive analysis of current data and case studies, this paper will highlight key challenges from a practical and ethical perspective. This paper will discuss the current state of AI in surgery, how it is being implemented currently, and its roles, regulations, and technical requirements. We will then delve into ethical concerns from patients' and medical professionals' perspectives, such as data privacy and security for patient confidentiality, professional autonomy and responsibility, equity and access for all patients, and patient safety. Additionally, we will cover the complex landscape of the practical limitations and regulations of using AI- the challenges of algorithmic interpretability, the implications of AI-driven automation in surgical contexts, and its impact on doctor-patient relationships. This paper aims to emphasize the importance of maintaining human oversight and empathy. Furthermore, we will discuss the future of AI in surgery, potential improvements, and how risks and concerns may be decreased. By analyzing the limitations, risks, and ethical dilemmas, this paper aims to provide insight into responsibly integrating AI in surgical care, creating a balance between technological advancement, patient-centered care and safety, and ethics.

articleTitle: Basic Medical Science Students Evaluation of Teaching Effectiveness: Careless Responses and its Consequences
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: This study aims to explore the carless responses (CR) in Basic Medical Science Students' Evaluation of Teaching Effectiveness (SET) and its consequences. Data was collected using a 20-item Likert scale survey with a sample size of 1280 Basic Medical Science students from the College of Medicine. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{z}$</tex> Person-fit statistic for polytomous items <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(l_z^p)$</tex> to detect careless responses in the Graded Response Model (GRM) was used in this study. The results of this study showed that Basic Medical Science Students' Evaluation of Teaching Effectiveness contains a high percentage of CRs (27.5%). CRs harm students' evaluation of their teachers' teaching effectiveness. These CRs decrease the mean of SET. Moreover., CRs decrease the validity of the SET survey. This means that the College of Medicine should have an action plan to detect and remove CRs from the SET dataset before doing the data analysis of SET and writing the reports.

articleTitle: Digital Devices in Mathematics Classes: A Negative Distraction or a Key to Success?
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The use of digital devices in the classroom is a contentious issue in many countries, especially after its extensive use during COVID-19. This research aimed to study the current status of the students regarding their use of digital devices. The study was conducted in one of the girls' schools. The sample consisted of 60 students from cycle 2 and 65 students from cycle 3. The study revealed that most of the students used 2 or 3 digital devices. The students also showed the most digital devices used are laptops and smartphones while smartwatches were the least. Results revealed that students use digital devices for leisure for a longer time than for learning. They also showed high levels of distraction while using digital devices as well as when their colleagues do. Interestingly, Cycle 2 students see the digital devices in mathematics classes as a key to success while Cycle 3 students see them as a negative distraction. As a result, there is a need to put policies in place at schools to control the use of digital devices and reduce the digital distraction that affects students') achievement in mathematics.

articleTitle: Detecting Myocardial Infraction in ECG Waveforms Using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The detection of myocardial infarction (MI) using advanced imaging and analysis techniques is a pivotal advance- ment in medical diagnostics. This study employs YOLOv8, a sophisticated deep learning algorithm, for the identification of MI from the electrocardiogram (ECG) images, focusing specifically on the critical ST elevation segment associated with MI. Unlike traditional methods that rely on manual interpretation, our approach automates the detection process, significantly reducing the time and potential for human error. By fine-tuning YOLOv8 on a curated dataset and employing a loss-modified model, we achieved an average accuracy of 96% and a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.99 at a 50% confidence threshold, with a Recall of 97.7%. To make this technology accessible to medical staff and patients without technical expertise, we developed a user-friendly GUI that simplifies the detection process by clicking a button. This research not only highlights the potential of applying deep learning in cardiology but also emphasizes the importance of user-centered design in medical technology, promising significant improvements in clinical diagnosis and patient care.

articleTitle: AI in Diagnostic Imaging: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Incorporating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into medical image diagnoses transforms medical diagnostics by improving efficiency, accuracy, and patient outcomes. AI claims huge assurance for promoting medical image diagnoses. However, its effective implementation necessitates attentive attention to practical and ethical issues. This paper provides an overview of the revolutionary influence of AI technologies on pathology and radiology, emphasizing the main improvements, advantages, and challenges that are considered to achieve their full potential.

articleTitle: Healthcare Super Apps and Streamlining Patient Management
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Healthcare super apps are all-encompassing solutions that combine various patient management tasks such as EHR, medication administration, and appointments. By integrating these services, super apps offer a comprehensive perspective of the patient's health, making it easier for healthcare givers to offer efficient and personalized care. This paper focuses on the barriers and determinates of patient portal adoption among patients and healthcare seekers.

articleTitle: On the Automatic Generation of Smart Contracts with Access Control for Digital Health
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Smart contracts automate medical workflows in healthcare blockchain-based applications. DAML, a smart contract language that supports cross-platform deployment with direct language features related to access control, has become more mainstream. To facilitate the development of DAML contracts, a higher-level modeling language (called iContractML) has been developed that allows the contract designers to diagrammatically define contracts. In this paper, we present a case study that utilizes an extended form of the iContractML language for the automatic DAML contract generation in the field of digital healthcare. The evaluation demonstrates that the generated contracts successfully implement all access control constraints; a core requirement to such healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Healthcare Delivery: A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Integrating Face-to- Face and Virtual Consultations
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Digital health (or telehealth) appears to be one of the most active areas of study in today's world and has been showing substantial evidence of effectiveness in different aspects of modern society. Most significantly, in the healthcare systems, where availability of quality services is the cornerstone, digital health solutions are transforming practices for patients. This paper proposes a mathematical model for healthcare systems in which a comprehensive approach is taken to patient need to be hospitalized. An objective function is established aiming to maximizing the number of patients needing hospitalization, either through face-to-face consultations or through online portals while taking into consideration the attitude of all patients towards online consultations. To achieve this, we use the preferences in the model to make sure that patient satisfaction is not compromised while resources are used efficiently. With a formal breakdown and analysis of the problem and considerable reliance on complex optimization algorithms, the model outlines a set of steps that will ensure the optimal distribution of patients in terms of face-to-face and virtual consultations. This in turn not only increases effectiveness of the healthcare delivery systems but it also improves the efficiency of the health care delivery systems as well. As a confirmation of our model, we tested it on an example data and used LINGO software to obtain the best solution of the problem. The findings from this example pinpoint the possibility of applying the model for developing effective solutions to patient distribution and, therefore, enhance the overall benefits of the healthcare system. This systematic approach is aimed at demonstrating the positive changes which are possible in the delivery of patient care through the introduction of technology supports in modern health care infrastructures.

articleTitle: COVID-19 Preventive Policy Preferences and Households Self-Reported Preventive Behaviors During the Pandemic: Evidence from Burkina Faso
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: This study proposes two novel indices of non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) against Covid-19, characterizing respectively household level self-directed voluntary and government-directed mandatory policy preferences; followed by a spatial analysis of their distributional properties across various sub-national levels, and the predictive modelling of their relationships with actual preventive behaviors. To this end, the study uses data on a cross-section of 1972 households from the 3rd wave of the 2020 Burkina Faso Covid-19 High Frequency Phone Survey, collected by its National Institute of Statistics and Demography, between September 12 and October 21, 2020. The findings revealed the significance of the two proposed indices for decentralized, socially sensitive policy making. With its statistically significant correlation coefficients, the multivariate probabilistic modelling showcased important household level's inter-dependence in adherence to NPIs across the considered preventive measures. Most importantly, it transpired that actual preventive behaviors are better motivated through self-directed voluntary measures, than government directed mandatory measures, as the latter is observed to reduce the likelihood of adherence to NPIs, while the former is seen to increase this likelihood. The findings also highlighted significant income based gradient in adherence behaviors, with the households identified above the official poverty threshold showing more adherence than those below the poverty line. On the other hand, social protection programs including food assistance, direct cash transfers, and other in-kind-transfers were all found to significantly increase the likelihood of adhering to NPIs. Since NPIs are the primary defense line during the early stages of a novel disease outbreak, when scientific knowledge is limited, and medical interventions are scarce, understanding society's preferences for NPIs provide insights for socially sensitive, preventive policy making.

articleTitle: Short VideoAddiction and Its Relationship with Students' Academic Achievement and Well-Being: A Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: This pilot study aimed to investigate the extent of short video addiction among students; identify the most popular social media platforms used to watch them; and determine the relationship between short video addiction and students' academic achievement and physical and mental health. This quantitative cross-sectional study used a web-based survey employing a questionnaire to collect data from 54 university students in the Arab Gulf region. The findings revealed a low extent of addiction to watching short videos, and that Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts are the most used platforms. The findings also revealed that short video addiction has no statistical relationship with students' academic achievement, while it has a statistically significant relationship with their physical and mental health. This study is one of the very few that address the risks of short video addiction in light of the excessive use of social media.

articleTitle: Supporting Quality of Life Decision Making for Treating Breast Cancer Patients Using an Integrated Quality of Life Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The rising incidence of breast cancer globally highlights the need to focus on quality of life (QoL) as a key outcome in patient care. QoL includes several dimensions, such as physical, psychological, social, and spiritual well-being, all of which can significantly affect treatment outcomes and patient satisfaction. This study aims to develop a comprehensive QoL framework for breast cancer patients to enhance personalized treatment approaches. Utilizing a Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM), we combined established quality of life (QoL) assessment tools, including the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30), the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Breast-Specific Module (EORTC QLQ-BR23), and the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Spiritual Well-Being Scale (FACIT-Sp-12), into a comprehensive framework. We conducted a survey of 88 breast cancer patients undergoing treatment at a tertiary hospital in Jordan, collecting demographic, clinical, and QoL data through self-administered questionnaires. Results: Developing a visualized, comprehensive QoL framework for both stakeholders and patients allowed them to examine the various QoL domains that influence patient well-being and their potential impact on treatment outcomes. The analysis revealed that cognitive ability, social support, and physical activity significantly affected patients' QoL. The mean global health score was 65.81, indicating moderate QoL levels. Notably, spirituality, as measured by FACIT-Sp scores, showed a positive correlation with overall QoL, suggesting that spiritual well-being plays an essential role in patient coping and satisfaction. This integrated QoL framework provides valuable insights into the multifaceted experiences of breast cancer patients, emphasizing the need for personalized care that considers physical, functional, psychological, and spiritual dimensions alongside clinical treatment. Future research should further explore the association between these domains and their implications for treatment adherence and long-term survivorship outcomes.

articleTitle: Distilling the Progress of Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Usage by Canadian Physicians
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The main objective of this study is to assess the Canadian record-keeping system, with a focus on the actual use of Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) by physicians in healthcare settings. The assessment is based on quantitative data collected from four national surveys conducted in 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2021 by the National Physician Survey (NPS), the Canadian Medical Association (CMA), and Canada Health Infoway (Infoway). Findings indicate that 86.6% of Canadian physicians were using EMRs in their daily practice in 2021, representing a five-and-a-half-fold increase since 2010. Regarding usage rates by primary care type, there is a statistically significant difference between Family Physicians/General Practitioners (FP/GP) and other specialists, with specialists reporting higher EMR use than FP/GPs. Canadian healthcare policymakers have addressed organizational and technical barriers faced by physicians, by building a shared national vision and leadership, and enhancing coordination among various stakeholders and levels of government.

articleTitle: Smart Endotracheal Intubation Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Endotracheal intubation (ETI) is an essential medical method employed to ensure the openness of the airway during acute diseases or anesthesia. Recent developments in airway management involve the incorporation of robotic technology together with a camera in the endotracheal tube. This study aims to automate a robot arm movement during endotracheal intubation by analyzing frames captured by an endoscopic camera, primarily focusing on classifying the larynx and trachea. Due to the unavailability of a publicly accessible dataset for these specific classes, the authors took the initiative to develop a dataset consisting of larynx and trachea images that were collected from videos recorded during endotracheal intubation of a medical manikin and from videos recorded during tracheal intubation for patients undergoing thyroidectomy which are available at: https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/anesthres1010003/s1. The created dataset was employed for the classification task using the MobileNetV2 convolutional neural network (CNN) model with transfer learning (TL). The results demonstrated high accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score levels in the performance evaluation of the testing set.

articleTitle: Legal Controls for Telemedicine Services and their Applications in the United Arab Emirates - An Analytical Study
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: This paper dealt with explaining the mechanism of using information technology means in providing medical services remotely, as it has become an important role in providing medical services due to the time and effort it saves for the doctor and the patient. Therefore, it was necessary to find a legal framework that regulates the practice of remote medical services. By establishing the necessary controls to provide it properly, safely and with high quality. It also dealt with a statement of the parties to remote medical services and the conditions that must be met to practice those services, and their obligations imposed on them by the Emirati legislator in order to ensure that they provide these services in the required manner. The most important remote medical services that can be provided to patients were also discussed, which are: remote diagnosis, consultation. Telemedicine, telemedicine prescription, remote medical monitoring. It became clear to us that remote medical services do not differ from the medical services that are provided traditionally, but their peculiarities lie in the means through which they are carried out. In order to develop remote medical services, it is necessary to conduct a periodic evaluation of the remote health care system used in the country. The state during certain regular periods of time, in order to ensure the quality and safety of the technology used in providing these services, and to ensure that electronic health systems are safe and not vulnerable to penetration and malfunctions that may affect them, in order to reduce their risks.

articleTitle: Smart Insulin Calculator: Technological Innovation for Type 1 Diabetes Management Revolutionising Insulin Management with Intelligent Health Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Type 1 Diabetes management demands precision, care, and adaptability, presenting significant challenges in daily life. This paper introduces an AI-powered application to revolutionise carbohydrate counting and insulin dose calculation for Type One Diabetes patients. Our app simplifies meal planning and insulin management by leveraging advanced algorithms and real-time data and offering personalised recommendations to sustain optimal blood glucose levels. This novel technological vision aims to enhance accuracy, reduce cognitive burden, and improve the quality of life for T1D patients. It welcomes the future of diabetes care with intelligent health technology that significantly impacts the quality of life of diabetes patients.

articleTitle: Jurisdiction of UAE Courts in Litigating International Digital Health Disputes
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: An analytical study of the rules of the international jurisdiction of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) Courts and its application to disputes related to digital health services to demonstrate appropriateness of these rules and assess the need to adjust them to suit the ongoing advancing technology and its application in digital health services. The study addresses applications of these rules such as determining the domicile in digital environment through two sections, the first examined the application of personal jurisdiction rules and the second addressed the challenges of applying these rules on digital health disputes.

articleTitle: Beyond Birth: Exploring the Complexities & Potential Misuse of Artificial Womb Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Artificial Womb Technology (AWT) promises revolutionary advancements in infertility treatments and neonatal care for premature infants. This paper conducts an examination of AWT's ethical, legal, social, environmental, economic, and cybersecurity implications. Methodologically, it integrates an extensive review of existing literature with a theoretical analysis of potential misuse patterns. The ethical discussion addresses concern about the commodification of human life, parental rights, and the disruption of natural birth processes. Legal challenges focus on the necessity for new regulations to govern usage, consent, and responsibility. Social implications highlight the potential impact on family dynamics and the risk of worsening existing inequalities, while the environmental considerations are centered on the resource demands, overpopulation and waste associated with AWT. Economically, AWT introduces new market opportunities while also raising concerns about commercialization and profit-driven misuse. Cybersecurity emerges as a critical, overlooked issue due to the sensitive nature of the data involved and the severe consequences of potential breaches. The theoretical analysis highlights the historical misuse patterns in digital health technologies, reinforcing the urgent need for stringent guidelines and policies to ensure the responsible implementation of AWT.

articleTitle: Shaping the Future of Healthcare: The Key Characteristics and Drivers of Smart Hospitals
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: this paper aims to explore and identify the key characteristics that define smart hospitals, as well as the primary drivers fostering the transformation of conventional hospitals into smart healthcare environments. As the healthcare sector continues to embrace technological innovation, smart hospitals are emerging as a critical model for improving patient care, efficiency, and accessibility. This paper anticipated to offer valuable insights for researchers and stakeholders in healthcare, guiding them in establishing the necessary framework or roadmap for the successful digital transformation of hospitals into smart, technology-driven systems..

articleTitle: Optimizing CLABSI Prediction: Data and Process Modeling Approach for Enhanced Model Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections (CLABSIs) are important Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAI) resulting in increased morbidity, mortality, and medical care costs. Data relevance, quality, and appropriateness are crucial characteristics for any effective and successful predictive model including CLABSI prediction. This study tackles the problem of finding out which among many possible features might be most representative or relevant to predict CLABSls by proposing a new objective method of selecting features; we integrate text mining techniques with process modeling thus making it possible for us to know objectively which amongst them are significant ones that should always reflect in any dataset used for CLABSI prediction. What our approach does is to enhance the strength and accuracy of predictive models by providing verified sets of features as shown by results achieved herein. Also, this research brings into focus such points like having validated data as well process models which may play a role in determining the readiness levels of CLABSI dataset at hospital settings.

articleTitle: Vocal Cords Detection Using Edge Detection and Machine Learning Filtration
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Automating endotracheal intubation (EI), a critical medical procedure required for lung ventilation, has gained significant attention in the realm of medical imaging and robotics. Central to the success of automated EI is the reliable detection and visualization of vocal cords, a step traditionally performed using laryngoscopy. This paper introduces a novel method for detecting and segmenting vocal cords in endoscopic images by leveraging advanced edge detection techniques combined with machine learning (ML) filters. This approach uniquely integrates geometric and textural features derived from contours identified in the image, distinguishing vocal cords with high precision and speed. Beyond automating EI, this methodology has broader applications, including the removal of foreign objects and facilitating tracheal endoscopy. This paper details the development of a specialized dataset and the implementation of the solution, emphasizing its algorithmic innovations. The results demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in improving the accuracy and efficiency of vocal cords detection, offering a repeatable strategy for similar medical imaging challenges.

articleTitle: Navigating the Landscape of Building an Educational Pathology Digital Slide Library: An Institutional Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Imagine reading a pathology slide on your laptop or office desktop as if you were peering through a microscope. In addition, you can annotate, mark significant fields, and consult a colleague from a distance in a matter of minutes. All of this is enabled by digital pathology. In the age of digital pathology, using digital pathology slides or whole slide images (WSI) is a novel method of teaching pathology to medical students and pathology residents. However, creating a digital pathology library or website is complex due to the numerous steps needed. Proper preparation and troubleshooting are required. We describe our experience building a digital pathology library for medical students, which can be accessed through a university website. This study focuses on Phase I of the initiative, which includes collecting cases, scanning, and archiving digital slides. We also discuss workflow, challenges, and solutions. Representative pathologic diagnoses were selected from the pathology department's database based on prevalence and educational value. High-quality slides were reviewed, digitised, labelled, and organised. Phase 2, which entails integrating the digital slide library into the university website and providing students access, is being established. In general, building a WSI library for teaching purposes entails several processes, including slide collection (collecting cases, determining slide acceptability for scanning, scanning slides), WSI storage, and website development and operation. A library of pathology digital slides was produced with considerable educational potential. The challenges faced, and possible solutions are also examined. Continuous maintenance and development are essential to transform medical students’ educational experiences.

articleTitle: Establishing Liability in Medical Malpractice Due to Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Based Diagnostic and Therapeutic Interventions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Determining liability if a patient suffers an injury due to AI or robotic application use is complex. The study used comparative legal analysis and examined the current legal frameworks and whether applying current principles of medical liability is adequate to determine liability arising from AI and robotics-related medical malpractice. The study identifies the gaps in current legislation and proposes applying new legal doctrines such as vicarious liability, custodian liability, corporate liability, strict liability, and finally, applying the benefit and burden rule. AI and robotics will revolutionize medical care. However, new legislation is necessary to mitigate risk and ensure patient safety.

articleTitle: Exploring the Value and Regulatory Perspectives of Artificial Intelligence ChatGPT in Pharmacoeconomic: A Qualitative Study on Benefits, Risks, and Stakeholder Beliefs
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Background: Growth in artificial intelligence systems can allow the automation of a crucial section of the traditional manual work practiced in pharmacoeconomics and evidence synthesis. However, artificial intelligence has a low autonomous analytical skill capabilities. The objective is to conduct a thematic analysis of the benefits and risks of applying ChatGPT across various sub-disciplines within pharmacoeconomics analysis. A purposive sampling technique was used to select the participants, utilizing the convenience sampling approach. All interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim, and thematic analysis was applied to identify themes within the data. The result shows that most of the respondents find AI ChatGPT helpful as it increases data analysis and processing efficiency, as well as improving real-time decision making. Additionally, the participants believe that information accessibility and dissemination are appealing features of AI ChatGPT. However, the respondents identified potential drawbacks in AI ChatGPT use, such as data quality and accuracy, contextual awareness limitations, privacy and security concerns, lack of responsibility and accountability, limitations in generalizability, social and ethical concerns, uncertainty understanding limitations, and amplification of bias. Employing ChatGPT in pharmacoeconomics presents significant potential for enhancing data processing efficiency, providing real-time decision support, and improving information accessibility for healthcare stakeholders. However, these benefits come with various risks and ethical challenges, including concerns about data accuracy, contextual awareness, security, accountability, generalizability, and potential bias amplification. By putting in place robust safeguards, adhering to ethical standards, and maintaining vigilant oversight, we can effectively leverage ChatGPT's potential while maintaining the principles of responsible, equitable, and ethical healthcare decision making.

articleTitle: Hospital Scheduling Systems Current Challenges and Emerging Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Hospital scheduling systems are integral components of healthcare management, addressing the complex challenge of optimizing appointment schedules. In the realm of healthcare research, the Appointment Scheduling Problem (ASP) has garnered significant attention due to its multifaceted nature. This problem is particularly pronounced in the outpatient setting, where effective scheduling systems can significantly impact patient satisfaction and overall health care efficiency. Recent comprehensive reviews highlighted the complexity of the Appointment Scheduling Problem within healthcare services, emphasizing the need for innovative solutions and proposing new scheduling models. This paper reviews literature on the topic of hospital scheduling systems, then looks into the current challenges prevalent in it and the emerging solutions that are discussed in literature. The review offers opportunities for innovation and improvements in scheduling procedures while highlighting difficulties with allocation of resources, appointment scheduling, and technology integration. Using advanced technologies into healthcare such as blockchain and AI-driven algorithms, are said to be integral to move in the direction of care that is patient-centric and efficient operations. The study highlights limitations in hospital scheduling systems, including scalability and generalizability, operational uncertainties, need for real-world implementation, and lack of consideration for emergency cases. To improve patient outcomes and the efficiency of healthcare scheduling, ongoing research and development, stakeholder involvement, user-centred design, and longitudinal research are essential. In summary, hospital scheduling systems represent a dynamic area of research, addressing the intricate interplay between patient satisfaction, resource optimization, and technological advancements.

articleTitle: Nurses' Knowledge and Perceptions of Telehealth After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Cross-Sectional Study from Jordan
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Background: Telehealth is an effective strategy for combating the COVID-19 pandemic and refers to the use of electronic communication to transfer health information across locations to enhance a patient's condition. Objective: This study aimed to assess knowledge and perceptions of telehealth technology among Jordanian nurses. These perceptions are about the advantages, disadvantages, necessity, ease of use, and security of telehealth technology. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey conducted among 252 nurses who worked in three Jordanian hospitals. Online Google forms distributed through social media platforms. Results: The study found that 56.3% of respondents were female, with an average age of 34 years, with the highest age group being 25–35. Most had less than 10 years of nursing experience. The findings of the study suggest that the nurses' knowledge of telehealth is moderate, and more than half of them had a positive perception of telehealth. The perception of the ease of use (3.48 ± 0.65) and technology's security (3.65± 0.62) found to have the most significant impact towards the use of telehealth. The nurses' age about knowledge of the telehealth technology (p =. 002) was significant. Conclusion: Exposure to telehealth after the pandemic increased nurse utilization. Moderate knowledge of nurses about telehealth affects their perceptions. Educating them about modern technologies like telehealth helps improve their understanding.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Applications in Surgical Video Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The surgical field has advanced much during the last two decades, based on continuous technological development that provided impressive improvements in terms of precision, efficiency, and patient care. Deep learning, a vital branch of artificial intelligence in surgical video processing, has been one of the significant and influential developments in this area. This paper reviews deep learning in surgical video processing applications and discusses performance, developments, challenges, and future research directions. It speaks of broad applications, including instrument detection, phase recognition, and video summarization, applied using various deep learning techniques. The review also underlines large, annotated datasets as a requirement to train robust models. While deep learning has taken huge strides within medicine, the paper acknowledges that computational complexity, model interpretability, and data privacy are some of the big challenges. Future perspectives are oriented toward explainable AI, synthetic data generation, and collaborative frameworks to extend deep learning clinically for better surgical efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Enhancing Speech Production Through AI-Game-Based Practice Activities in the UAE Schools
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of game-based learning interventions in enhancing the oral communication abilities, including accuracy, fluency, and coherence, of primary Emirati students in grades four and five. The focus is specifically on English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teaching in schools in the UAE. This study aims to overcome the shortcomings of conventional drills, which often struggle to properly rectify initial speech mistakes. To do this, a controlled experimental design is used, comprising a total of 1,000 students who are separated into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group engaged in game-based learning activities, while the control group adhered to traditional teaching approaches. The pre-and post-intervention evaluations were examined using descriptive and inferential statistics, specifically t-tests. The results showed that the experimental group saw considerable increases. Accuracy rose by 31.6%, fluency by 34.2%, and coherence by 36.9%. These results highlight the greater effectiveness of game-based learning compared to conventional approaches and also address the lack of study on the impact of interactive learning on UAE EFL learners. This research advocates for the widespread incorporation of game-based techniques into educational curriculum, which has the potential to revolutionize teaching methods and improve student engagement and learning results in language education.

Index Terms: Schools In The United Arab Emirates

articleTitle: Exploring the Value and Risks of Artificial Intelligence ChatGPT in Infectious Disease Management and Public Health: Regulatory Perspectives and Qualitative Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Background: The goal of this work is to perform a thematic analysis of the advantages and disadvantages towards employing ChatGPT in different subfields of Infectious Disease (ID) and public health. Currently, the research adopts a qualitative research approach. The interview guide was developed using a structured literature review having semi-structured interview questions. Twenty-five epidemiologists participated this study, which were selected purposively through convenience sampling technique. The interviews conducted were audio taped, transcribed and verbatim and the data was analyzed using thematic analysis to establish themes in the data. Hence, analysing the positives of using the AI ChatGPT: Eight themes and 28 were codes deduced at the end of the first part of the thematic analysis. The risks of using AI ChatGPT in this field were identified and they were grouped into ten themes and thirty codes. Some of the advantages of AI ChatGPT are well seen in these areas taking into consideration specific health recommendations, the contribution towards clinical decision-making processes, and in the process of vigilance in outbreaks. However, the potential risks include the creation of fake news, privacy violation, and dependency of the AI system are some of the concerns that should be critically followed in the implementation. Future studies should target the improvement of the data acquisition of ChatGPT in real-time, the extension of its medical content in novel diseases and the use of context-aware suggestions.

articleTitle: Navigating the Digital Landscape: Telemedicine and e-Health Utilisation in Non-Communicable Diseases in the Arab World: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), such as hypertension and diabetes, are major health problems across the world, particularly in Arab countries and those with limited access to healthcare services. Telemedicine allows doctors to treat patients remotely, increasing efficiency by evenly distributing healthcare resources. Because of the region's peculiar socioeconomic and political context, the rapid implementation of electronic health care presents both significant advantages and challenges. This comprehensive, systematic search aims to collect data on telemedicine implementation in the Arab world, evaluating its performance, limitations, and prospective solutions for enhancing telehealth services. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review of the literature looking for full-text primary studies that evaluated NCDs treated by telemedicine, regardless of research design, published in English from 2009 to July 2024 in three main databases: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library. Rayyan software enabled the screening process, and to ensure a thorough search, we reviewed the bibliographies of the identified publications. The studies were evaluated using the Measuring Tool to Assess Systematic Review 2 (AMSTAR 2). The search resulted in 211 studies, with 25 being included. The findings indicate widespread agreement on the advantages of telemedicine and its contribution to improved community health. However, a number of challenges and barriers arose throughout the implementation process, including connection issues and limited online access to healthcare due to insufficient infrastructure, a lack of collaboration among healthcare resources, and cost constraints. Policymaking, infrastructure, and healthcare practices must be improved to guarantee the efficient and fair implementation of telemedicine services in Arab countries. This study is pending final registration for PROSPERO (the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews).

articleTitle: Transforming Healthcare in Jordan: Enhancing the Patient Journey with AI Innovations Using AI to Enhance Patient Experiences and Hospital Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) ushers in a new age in healthcare, presenting tremendous prospects to improve patient care and simplify hospital operations. This article investigates the revolutionary potential of AI in improving the patient journey in Jordanian hospitals, emphasising emergency departments. We propose a unique AI application currently in development to assist in rapidly identifying diseases and efficiently redirecting patients to suitable departments, reducing the pressure on emergency services. Following a thorough analysis of the available literature, we discovered substantial gaps in research on the implementation of AI in Jordan's healthcare system. Our examination of information from Jordan's Ministry of Health highlights the critical need for AI solutions to solve the country's hospitals' particular difficulties. This study emphasises the vital role of AI in improving patient experiences and optimising resource utilisation. Still, it also advocates for targeted research to fully reap the benefits of AI-driven healthcare advances in Jordan.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning Models for Classification of Inhalation and Exhalation in Respiratory Cycles Using Thermal Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Breathing Pattern Disorders (BPD) significantly impact the quality of life for many individuals, particularly those suffering from asthma and anxiety-related conditions. These disorders can lead to chronic respiratory issues, reduced physical performance, and heightened psychological stress. Therefore, accurately detecting and monitoring breathing patterns is crucial for effectively managing and treating BPD. To address this issue, this paper proposes several deep learning models, including DenseNet121, VGG16, ResNet152V2, InceptionV3, and NAS-NetMobile, to classify inhalation and exhalation phases within respiratory cycles using thermal imaging. By leveraging transfer learning, distinct breathing patterns, including long, normal, and rapid cycles, were effectively identified from thermal signatures. We have evaluated the performance of the proposed deep learning models using a labeled thermal image dataset. The results show the effectiveness of the proposed models, specifically VGG16 and DenseNet121, which demonstrated high classification accuracies of 96% and 93%, respectively. This non-invasive approach enhances diagnostic capabilities in detecting and monitoring BPD. The integration of automated image classification into respiratory analysis offers a promising tool for healthcare professionals to assess respiratory health and potentially preempt clinical deterioration through early intervention.

articleTitle: “Ethical Challenges and Solutions in AI-Powered Digital Health”
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: Addressing ethical issues in AI advancements is crucial for ensuring positive contributions to healthcare without compromising ethical standards and patient trust. This paper explores the ethical challenges around the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in digital health, focusing on data privacy, algorithmic bias, and transparency in autonomy. Therefore, the results show the existing issues of data vulnerability, including patient data leakage, stressing the importance of strong data protection mechanisms. Cases of bias in handling AI algorithms were pointed out primarily resulting in the inequality of health care provision, and hence the need to build better training data and techniques for bias elimination. The inability to reveal how and why an AI solution reached a particular conclusion undermines the patient's confidence in a given product or service, which is where the concepts of explainable AI and accountability come in. Ethical concerns regarding data privacy and trust erosion in medical practice are a growing concern. A qualitative study reveals significant gaps in existing literature on AI ethics in healthcare. the paper highlights key recommendations include enhanced regulatory frameworks, robust data protection measures, and increased transparency in AI algorithms to manage these ethical concerns. These solutions aim to ensure that the use of AI in healthcare is well-controlled, enhancing the healthcare system while respecting patient rights. Key funding and contributions from well-wishers have been instrumental in supporting this research, providing resources and insights essential for addressing these critical ethical challenges.

articleTitle: Cyber Risk and Threat Assessment Against the Security of Medical Devices and the Internet of Medical Things - A Theoretical Proposal
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a detailed theoretical study proposal to assess the cyber risks and threats against the security of medical devices and the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) in hospitals. The main objective of this study is to provide a practical project proposal to gain more information and insights into the world of medical devices and the Internet of Medical Things and their cybersecurity and to identify where efforts should be made to protect medical devices and patients. This paper provides details of experimental design, strategy, and methods. The relationship between the risk to patient's health, data sensitivity, Level of connectivity, Level of Authentication, the Impact of a breach, Updatability Potential & Downtime, Interoperability, and Environmental threats - as independent variables, and overall security and safety score - as dependent variables, will be investigated. Ethical considerations and procedures are also properly considered, and some proactive suggestions are provided.

articleTitle: Streamlining CLABSI Diagnosis: An Innovative Process Modeling Approach Using UML Activity Diagrams
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: This paper presents the development and validation of a Unified Modeling Language (UML) Activity Diagram for diagnosing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections (CLABSIs) based on guidelines from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN). The activity diagram translates complex guidelines into an accessible visual model, refined through iterative feedback from domain experts in healthcare and software engineering. This tool aims to enhance understanding, adherence, and education regarding CLABSI diagnosis, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy and consistency. Additionally, the diagram serves as a foundation for developing software applications to automate the detection and diagnosis of CLABSIs, further enhancing clinical efficiency and patient outcomes. By providing a clear and structured process model, this study contributes significantly to the field of healthcare informatics and patient safety.

articleTitle: Knowledge Management Practices Among Medical Students: An Investigation of Knowledge Creation, Acquisition, Sharing, and Capture
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Digital Health Knowledge Exchange & Empowerment Conference (gDigiHealth.KEE)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate knowledge management practices among medical students. The study attempted to find out demographic differences among students concerning knowledge creation, acquisition, sharing, and capture. The study implemented the survey method through an online questionnaire using Google Forms for data collection. A total of 340 medical students from 11 medical colleges in India participated in the survey. The collected data was analyzed using Microsoft Excel and SPSS v23. Statistical tests such as t-tests and ANOV A tests were performed to validate the stated hypotheses. The findings of the study have reported how medical students with different demographic backgrounds differ in knowledge management practices. Of the five demographic criteria investigated, medical students demonstrated age group differences, differences in educational level, and geographical location differences in knowledge management practices. The findings of the study suggested the impact of age, educational level, and geographical location on knowledge creation, acquisition, and capturing. On the other hand, gender and work experience appeared to have no influence on knowledge management practices among medical students. There are limited studies conducted in India on knowledge management practices among medical students. This study could be one of the important contributions from India reporting medical students' involvement in knowledge creation, acquisition, sharing, and capturing. Medical colleges and institutions in India should ensure that KMP activities, particularly knowledge creation, acquisition, sharing, and capturing, are integrated into medical courses and curricula.
